messages:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED PAGE -> latency.autopage p95/p99 spike detected in eu-west-1. PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345. Threshold: p99 > 1200ms for 5m. Autopage fired for rotation 'oncall-eu'.
PagerDuty: Page fired to Oncall Rotation (priority: P1).
Alex C: acked via PagerDuty. I'm on it — looking at dashboards.
Sara J: thanks, ping if you need extra hands.
Alex C: quick summary from metrics: p95 ~ 400ms, p99 ~ 1600-2200ms, error rate still low. Tail dominated by model-side long queues (queue depth spiking on a subset of hosts).
Maya P: seeing large KV cache miss rates on the same shard group, hotkeying suspected.
Alex C: confirming kvcache metrics, host group kube-eu-infer-5 shows KV miss rate 98% for minute window.
ops-bot: autoscaler suggested +3 replicas to handle burst; current pool at 8.
Alex C: initiating a reactive scale: kubectl scale deploy/inference-eu --replicas=11; log paste: ```Scaled deployment "inference-eu" to 11 replicas```
Sara J: can we also temporarily route traffic off the noisy hosts?
Alex C: doing a quick cordon + drain on kube-eu-infer-5 to bounce the process: ```kubectl cordon kube-eu-infer-5 && kubectl drain kube-eu-infer-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```
Maya P: adding a reroute rule to smart-router for 60s to avoid that host group: ```POST /routing/override { "avoid_hosts": ["kube-eu-infer-5"], "ttl": 60 }```
Alex C: applied reroute. Observability note: KV cache hit ratio on the shard improved from 2% -> 45% after routing change and scale.
Alex C: p99 dropped to ~900ms within 90s after actions, p95 back to ~320ms. Still above baseline but trending down.
PagerDuty: Pager acknowledged. Escalation suppressed (no further escalation while acknowledged).
Sara J: what about requester-side batching? Any rogue large batch sizes?
Maya P: logs show some clients sending unusual max_seq 4096 requests hitting the hotkey. Filtering rule added at edge: max_seq <= 2048 for now.
Alex C: edge filter applied. Also enabling request-level evictions for KV cache on that shard to avoid thrash: ```curl -X POST https://ops.api/cache/evict -d '{"shard":"eu-west-1-7","evict_percent":20}'```
ops-bot: eviction job scheduled, will run in 30s.
Alex C: recheck metrics: tail tokens per request decreased and the queue latency for the hot shard started to fall. p99 now ~480ms.
Maya P: customer impact: a few customers with long-context requests may have experienced slow responses for ~6 minutes. No 5xx spike, mostly high tail latency.
Sara J: opening a short incident note for CS: "Short p99 latency spike in eu-west-1; mitigations applied (scale + reroute + edge filter); customers using >4k seq may have seen degraded latency for ~6m)."
Alex C: added runbook steps and timeline to incident tracker INC12345.
PagerDuty: Auto-escalation timer cleared; rotation will be notified if further alerts fire.
Maya P: follow-up: we should consider a hotkey detector in the router to proactively identify high-token flows and route them to a dedicated pool. Filing infra ticket INFRA-771.
Sara J: agree. Also add a Canary for KV missrate alarms so we get earlier warnings.
Alex C: handoff to next oncall: @Oncall Rotation — current state: p99 stable ~450ms, reroute TTL 60s (expires soon), eviction job completed, scaled to 11 replicas. Please monitor for recurrence and consider bumping routing TTL if it flaps.
Oncall Rotation: thanks @Alex C, @Sara J, @Maya P — taking over. I'll keep INC12345 open and do a post-incident note if it stays stable.
Alex C: leaving one last note — affected shard: eu-west-1-7, probable cause: hotkeying from a small set of clients sending long sequences. Root-cause analysis ticket linked in INC12345.
Sara J: thx team, nice quickwave mitigation. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC12345 marked as "stabilized". If latency rises above threshold again, a new autopage will fire.
Oncall Rotation: monitoring — will escalate if new pages arrive.
